target.title: fix(agent-core): resolve tool-name mismatches for Claude Code alias calls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agents trained on Claude Code emit tool names such as `KnowledgeSearch`, `Glob`, `Agent`, and `Grep`. These names don't exist in a stock OpenClaw runtime, producing `Tool X not found` errors and causing the model to retry the same call until it gives up.

LCM corpus analysis on a private deployment (2026-03-15 – 2026-07-01):

| Tool name called | Failures |
|---|---|
| KnowledgeSearch | 2,586 |
| Glob | 1,234 |
| Agent | 429 |
| Grep | 159 |
| **Total** | **5,558 across 1,804 conversations** |

Representative failure trace (redacted):
```
tool_call   toolCallId=[redacted]  toolName=Agent  arguments={"prompt":"[redacted]"}
tool_result toolCallId=[redacted]  toolName=Agent  isError=true
            content=[{"type":"text","text":"Tool Agent not found"}]
```
The model retried twice more with the same tool name, got the same error, and gave up.

## Fix

Add `resolveToolAlias()` before the deferred-tool resolver in `resolveToolCallTool()`:

1. **Case-insensitive exact match** — catches capitalisation drift (e.g. `READ` → `Read`).
2. **Normalised alias map** — strips non-alphanumeric characters, then tries ordered fallback names:
   - `KnowledgeSearch` → `memory_search`, `knowledge_search`, `wiki_search`, `search`
   - `Glob` → `find`
   - `Agent` / `Task` → `sessions_spawn`
   - `Grep` → `grep`

When no alias matches, the not-found error now lists the agent's available tool names, which helps both the model self-correct and operators diagnose missing tool registrations.

The original tool-call name is preserved in the trajectory and tool-result audit identity so sessions are replay-identical to the pre-fix behaviour, except the call succeeds instead of erroring.

## Tests

Three new tests in the deferred-tool hydration suite (`agent-loop.test.ts`):

- `KnowledgeSearch` dispatches to `memory_search`
- Case-insensitive lookup (`FIND` → `find`)
- Not-found error includes available tool list

All 19 tests in `agent-loop.test.ts` pass locally (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.test.ts`).

## Evidence

**Before (pre-patch):** 5,558 `Tool * not found` failures in LCM across 1,804 conversations (full corpus, 2026-03-15 – 2026-07-01) — see the table above.

**After (post-patch):** the fix has been running as a local dist patch on a private OpenClaw deployment since 2026-07-02T14:43. Gateway restart at 2026-07-03T03:14 picked it up cleanly.

Post-restart grep of `gateway.log` (499 lines of live fleet traffic since restart):
```
$ grep -c 'Tool .* not found' ~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log \
    | since 2026-07-03T03:14
0
```

Post-restart grep of agent-trajectory files (`~/.openclaw/agents/*/sessions/*.jsonl`) for `toolName` matching any alias (Agent/Task/KnowledgeSearch/Glob/Grep) with a ts >= 2026-07-03:
```
0 events
```

Note: the private fleet also applies a billing-proxy `promptAppend` mitigation that steers model calls toward native tool names, which is why organic alias-name calls no longer appear in the post-patch gateway log even before this fix's alias resolution kicks in. The resolver fix removes the need for the prompt-level workaround entirely and provides a correct fallback for deployments that don't apply such mitigations — the ones producing those 5,558 pre-patch failures. An auto-harvester (LaunchAgent, hourly) on the private fleet will attach a real dispatch trace to this PR the first time a model drifts and emits an alias call, but the mitigation currently suppresses that on our side.

## Redactions

Chat IDs, topic IDs, tool call IDs, agent identifiers, task content, session keys, file paths under the private deployment.
